title.en: If–then and if and only if

body.en: The implication p → q ("if p then q") is false only when p is true and q is false. Its converse is q → p, its inverse is ~p → ~q, and its contrapositive is ~q → ~p. A statement and its contrapositive always have the same truth value; so do the converse and the inverse. The biconditional p ↔ q ("p if and only if q") is true when p and q have the same truth value. *Quantifiers*: "for all" (∀) and "there exists" (∃).

points.en: p → q false only for T → F
Converse and inverse may differ in truth

title.en: Four ways to validate a statement

say.en: Direct: assume p, reason step by step to q.
Contrapositive: assume not q and show not p.
Contradiction: assume p and not q together, and reach something impossible.
To show a statement is false, one counter-example is enough.

text.en: 4. Counter-example: one case where p is true and q false.
e.g. "every prime is odd": 2 is a counter-example.

say.en: Four ways to validate a statement.

body.en: To show "p and q" is true, show both; for "p or q", show one (or show that if p is false then q is true). For p → q: (1) direct method: assume p true and deduce q; (2) contrapositive: assume q false and deduce p false; (3) contradiction: assume p true and q false and reach an impossibility. A single counter-example shows that a "for all" statement is false. Example: √2 is irrational is proved by contradiction (assume √2 = a/b in lowest terms; both a and b come out even).

points.en: Examples, however many, do not prove "for all"

problem.en: Write the converse, inverse and contrapositive of "If a triangle is equilateral, then it is isosceles", and say which are true.

steps.en: Converse: If a triangle is isosceles, then it is equilateral. (False)
Inverse: If a triangle is not equilateral, then it is not isosceles. (False)
Contrapositive: If a triangle is not isosceles, then it is not equilateral. (True, like the original)

answer.en: The original and contrapositive are true; the converse and inverse are false

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Write the converse, inverse and contrapositive of "If a triangle is equilateral, then it is isosceles", and say which are true.

say.en: Let us solve this together. Write the converse, inverse and contrapositive of "If a triangle is equilateral, then it is isosceles", and say which are true.
Converse: If a triangle is isosceles, then it is equilateral. False.
Inverse: If a triangle is not equilateral, then it is not isosceles. False.
Contrapositive: If a triangle is not isosceles, then it is not equilateral. (True, like the original).
So the answer is The original and contrapositive are true; the converse and inverse are false.

problem.en: Show by a counter-example that "For every real x, x² > x" is false.

steps.en: Take x = 1/2: x² = 1/4, which is not greater than 1/2.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Show by a counter-example that "For every real x, x² > x" is false.

say.en: Let us solve this together. Show by a counter-example that "For every real x, x squared is greater than x" is false.
Take x equals 1 over 2: x squared equals 1 over 4, which is not greater than 1 over 2.
One counter-example is enough.
So the answer is x equals 1 over 2 (or x equals 0, or x equals 1).
